deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematical derivation. It is an administrative record of the sessions of the Göttingen mathematical-physical seminar run by W. Weber, in which Riemann served as assistant. It lists dated sessions and the written assignments (Aufgaben) taken on by students. It continues the list on the previous page (1 May to 19 June). The year is very probably 1855: the next page drafts a book order mentioning 'Clausthal 1855' and Riemann's 'late father', who died in 1855.

The page begins by finishing assignment 4 from the previous page: 'Über die Bestimmung der Con-[stanten] des Bifilarmagnetometers'. It is based on a paper by Hofrat Gauss in the 'Resultate aus den Beobachtungen des magnetischen Vereins' published in 1841 (cf. the session of 22 May), and is marked 'übernommen von Riemann'. So Riemann himself took on the written treatment of the constants of the bifilar magnetometer.

Sessions listed:
- 26 June: continuation of the 19 June lecture on transverse vibrations of elastic rods.
- 3 July: barometric measurement of the height of the Kleper (Kleperberg near Göttingen).
- 10 July: report on that height measurement. Experiments on how the extension modulus depends on the strain, using vulcanised rubber. The marginal insertion speaks of the 'change of the relation which for infinitely small extensions becomes equal to' the elastic modulus, i.e. the stress-strain relation dσ/dε → E as ε → 0. Also Ritter's lecture on transverse vibrations of a stretched string (cf. 19 June).
- 17 July: determination of Young's modulus from bending experiments on a rod, using mirror-and-scale (Poggendorff) reading.
- 24 July: experiments on cooling rate with a Breguet bimetallic-strip thermometer. Its curvature was measured by the mirror-and-scale method of 17 July.

The only conceptual content is implicit:
- the bifilar restoring torque, roughly (m g a b / l)·sin φ, balanced against the magnetic torque;
- the barometric height formula, h = (R T / (M g))·ln(p0/p);
- linear elasticity as the small-strain limit of a nonlinear stress-strain curve for rubber;
- the beam-bending deflection formula;
- bimetal curvature as a function of temperature.
None of these is worked out on the page.
errors: No derivations are present, so there are no mathematical errors to assess.

results.what: Theory and constants of the bifilar magnetometer, following Gauss (Resultate ... des magnetischen Vereins, 1841); Riemann assigned himself the write-up
Strain dependence of the extension modulus of vulcanised rubber; the linear modulus as the small-strain limit
results.usually_credited_to: Gough, Joule (rubber thermoelasticity); later Mooney-Rivlin theory

results.what: Young's modulus from rod flexure read with mirror and scale
results.modern_name: Beam-bending determination of Young's modulus; Poggendorff mirror reading

results.what: Cooling rate measured with a Breguet bimetallic thermometer
results.modern_name: Bimetallic strip thermometer / Newton's law of cooling

deep.surprise_reason: This is an administrative seminar protocol, not research. Riemann's role in Weber's mathematical-physical seminar is known. The mildly interesting details are that he took on the bifilar-magnetometer constants himself and that a rubber nonlinear-elasticity experiment was run in 1855. Neither is mathematically novel.

checkable.asserts: Isothermal barometric height formula, the standard basis of a barometric height measurement (context only; not written on the page).
Central deflection of a simply supported rectangular rod, from which E is obtained in bending experiments (context only).
The tangent modulus of the stress-strain relation tends to Young's modulus for infinitely small strains, as in the marginal note on rubber.
Approximate restoring torque of a bifilar suspension (wire separations a, b; length l) for small wire inclination (context only).

transcription_corrections: First line: '[?]theorie[?] des Bifilarmagnetometers' should read '-stanten des Bifilarmagnetometers'. It completes '4) Über die Bestimmung der Con-' from the previous page, i.e. 'Über die Bestimmung der Constanten des Bifilarmagnetometers'.
'in den Res-[-sult-] aus den Beob.' reads as 'in den Res-[-ult-] aus den Beob.'; the intended title is 'Resultate aus den Beobachtungen des magnetischen Vereins'.
Marginal insertion: the struck word is likely 'Extensionsmodulus' rather than 'Elasticitätsmodulus'. A deleted fragment 'wenn so grosse Dehnungen' is also present.
'{+zu denen [?] mittelst+}' is probably 'zu denen [der] Spiegel ...', i.e. 'bending experiments for which mirror and scale were used'.
